daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The DPR came under criticism as civil society groups accused lawmakers of drafting the Asset Forfeiture Bill non-transparently, with the draft yet to be opened for public review. Separately, the government's data verification process faced scrutiny as Central Java's Social Affairs Office announced it would re-verify 163,839 social assistance recipients after their data was flagged as potentially linked to online gambling. Meanwhile, the Statistics Agency (BPS) was ordered to complete corrections to mismatched decile data within a maximum of two weeks.

  • National Police Chief led a handover ceremony in which Komjen Fadil Imran retired and Brigjen Hengki was appointed as the new Papua Barat police chief.
  • DPR member Habiburokhman noted that asset forfeiture laws in the US, UK, and Australia do not solely target corruption cases.
  • The Attorney General twice invoked the phrase "the storm will surely pass" when addressing subordinates.
  • Villages and Regional Development Minister Yandri Susanto met former President Jokowi in Solo to personally deliver an invitation to his child's wedding reception.
  • Police confirmed they only requested assistance from the TNI and the Jakarta provincial government after GRIB helped disperse demonstration crowds.
  • Minister of State Apparatus Empowerment stated that the new Trade Corporate University will become a machine for producing excellent civil servants in the trade sector.
  • The replacement of the North Sulawesi police chief was described as organizational refreshment.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Eight Indonesian nationals joined the Russian military as mercenaries, reportedly lured by high-paying job offers that came with severe consequences. The Ministry of Law and Human Rights clarified that serving in a foreign army is among nine grounds for losing Indonesian citizenship. A tugboat capsized in Busan waters, leaving one dead and six missing including an Indonesian national.

  • Indonesia's ambassador to Algeria presented credentials to President Tebboune, with the Algerian leader stating his country is ready to prioritize investments from Indonesia.
  • Indonesia called on the Non-Aligned Movement to build the future rather than be trapped in the romanticism of the past.
  • Indonesian students in Vladivostok carried the red-and-white flag to welcome President Prabowo's arrival.
  • The Deputy Minister of Migrant Worker Protection stated that the SMK Go Global program is a bridge to international labor markets.

Other

Airline ticket prices are set to become more expensive, adding to consumers' cost burdens. The Indonesia Stock Exchange postponed the implementation of the Rp 1 minimum share price, citing specific regulatory considerations. Construction of an electric railway from Ngurah Rai Airport to Canggu is set to begin soon.

  • Thirteen banks have closed operations through September 2026.
  • Following the mass poisoning of 566 students, the head of SPPG faces possible dismissal, while the Ministry of Religious Affairs scrutinized the quality and supervision of government-provided food for Islamic boarding schools.
  • Indonesia is assessing CPO supply for B60 biodiesel rollout planned for 2027.
  • The government announced plans to develop 40,000 mini aquaculture systems with Australia.
  • Indonesia targets the placement of 500,000 migrant workers by 2029.
